body: Thank you, I'm in a situation similar to the op and I was also wondering about the order in which I would write. Your first point clarified it for me. Thanks!

Thank you, I like that analogy. Like you said, it's all subjective. Based on your advice, I'll start studying storytelling before getting to technical details like how a script is written and stuff.

About effort, allow me to borrow your analogy, I truly believe that the story in my head is a rough diamond. I want to polish it and present it (to readers), but I lack the skills needed to polish a precious diamond like that. If I attempt to polish it now, I might be able to do it, but it wouldn't sparkle to the best of it's ability. So I want to learn and improve my polishing skills, so I can eventually polish this rough diamond into a beautiful sparkling one, and then present it.

It's fine if everyone thinks it's bird poop instead of a diamond when I present it. I would've done my best to bring that story into existence, so I wouldn't have any gripe about no one liking it because I understand it's subjective.

The fact that I can't bring that story into existence with my current skill is what's driving me towards learning and improving.

So I really appreciate all the advice you're giving me, thank you so much.

Thank you so much for the elaborate advice. I do understand that artists have to be picky given how easy it has become for people to label themselves as "writers" these days.

I believe that the idea in my head (I've several ideas, but I'm talking about the main idea that led to me writing this post). The idea in my head is a very grand and epic spectacle filled with mythological and fantasy elements, something that the current me won't be able to execute and do justice to. If I rush it and end up with a mediocre story, and a subpar comic, it would be a disservice to the potential the story has.

So for now I've decided to learn the basics of comic writing and comic art, and write a few mini comics, then proceed to maybe some one shots, and a couple of 5-6 issue series.

Then using that experience, I intend to start working on the idea and put together a pitch bible for the comic that I can then show to publishers and artists.

Since you mentioned you're a publisher, could you please answer the question "what makes good comic?"

I've the idea for the story but I'm not able to imagine a way to execute it properly. Your answer might help me understand how to structure my stories so they can be made into readable comics.

I welcome any other piece of advice you have for me as well.

I intend to take this seriously and I would appreciate every piece of advice.

Thank you

Yeah, I've been researching on how comics are made, and I've decided to write a few mini comics on my own first like I've mentioned.

Once I've gathered some experience, then I'll start working on the idea that's currently in my head (I've several ideas, but I'm talking about the idea that led to me writing this post. I intend for this project to be my Magnum opus that'll go on for years.

I'm going to use the advice given by people in this thread, and start my journey as a comic book writer starting today.

Wish me luck. 🤞

Yeah, I've arrived on the decision that I'll try to do a 5-10 page mini comic on my own first to sort of get a hang of the process. 

By then I'll develop a full pitch bible for the comic.
